name: Facet
text: Ship a live contrast checker that runs before any submission. It flags low-contrast text or UI elements in real time, forcing fixes before the work leaves our hands. This guarantees visibility and clarity—key for a dark-themed, interactive interface—by catching accessibility issues early, when they’re cheap to fix. The trade-off is a small delay in submission, but that’s negligible compared to the cost of a broken user experience.

name: Pane
text: A live checker before submission treats contrast as a gatekeeper, but it risks slowing designers down when they’re iterating fast—especially in dark themes where contrast is harder to judge by eye. Instead, ship a live checker that runs *after* each major design change, not before submission, and pair it with a contrast heatmap overlay that updates in real time. That balances speed with visibility without forcing designers to fix issues they haven’t finalized yet.
